text: In this tutorial you write your first model-to-model transformation: two JjTL rules that turn the People model of the ER language into tables, columns and foreign keys.

Step one. The target metamodel, Relational, is built as in tutorial one. A Table owns its Columns through a composition. A Column has a name, a type from the SqlType enumeration and a primary key flag. A ForeignKey points at a source table and a target table.

Step two. Open the transformation, with ERD as source and Relational as target. The first rule reads: for every Entity create a Table, and copy its name. Validate, then Execute: pick the People model, keep the output name, and run. Three tables, and nothing else yet.

Step three. Columns live inside tables. The rule names the feature columns and creates one Column per attribute with forall. A value mapping turns the ER type into the SQL type, and the key flag becomes the primary key. Execute again: every table owns its columns, and the id columns are primary keys.

Step four. A Relationship becomes a ForeignKey. Left and right are entities, but source and target expect tables: the executor resolves them through the trace, whatever the order of the rules. Execute once more, this time naming the output PeopleSchema. Two foreign keys, pointing at tables.

Step five. Back in the editor, the Trace tab lists every rule application with its bindings, and the Output tab reports the run and any warning. Save the project: the schema is a model like any other.
